entities.name: Kruto the Wend
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Kruto the Wend, whose precise parentage is debated but is often linked to Grin or Grinus, rose to prominence as a formidable prince of Wagria and the broader Obotrite confederation in the late 11th century, dying in 1105. His significance lies in his successful, albeit temporary, consolidation of Wendish power against the encroaching Christianization and territorial ambitions of the Saxons and Danes, marking a critical period of pagan resurgence and resistance in the southern Baltic region. James Westfall Thompson's scholarship suggests his family may have belonged to the Rani of Rugia, underscoring his deep roots within the West Slavic aristocracy.

Kruto's ascent involved a direct challenge to the established Christianized Obotrite leadership, most notably the assassination of Prince Henry of the Obotrites (Heinrich, son of Gottschalk) around 1093. This act enabled Kruto to seize control of the Obotrite realm, establishing his authority from his stronghold in Oldenburg (Starigard) and reversing decades of Christian influence. Under his rule, pagan cults were restored, churches were destroyed, and German settlers were expelled, effectively creating a pagan Wendish state that held sway over much of modern-day Mecklenburg and Holstein for over a decade. He successfully repelled multiple Saxon incursions, solidifying a period of relative independence for the West Slavs.
